title: An Efficient Method for Adenovirus Production
protocol: Use a separate cell culture hood for adenoviral manipulations.
Use T flasks with filter caps for viral packaging and amplification.
Empty the cell culture hood after each use.
Expose the empty cell culture hood to UV light for 15 min.
Autoclave periodically the pipette aid, pipettes, and other utensils.
Culture AD293 cells for adenoviral packaging in a separate laboratory or hood if possible.
Check batches of different adenoviruses amplified in the same period for cross-contamination by PCR.
Mix 20 g of tryptone, 5 g of yeast extract, 0.5 g of NaCl, and 2.5 mL of 1 M KCl with H2O to make 1 L of SOB medium.
Autoclave the SOB medium at 121 °C.
Add 5 mL of 1 M MgCl2 and 5 mL of 1 M MgSO4 to the autoclaved SOB medium.
Mix 20 mL of 1 M glucose, 5 mL of 1 M MgCl2, and 5 mL of 1 M MgSO4 with 1 L of sterile SOB medium to prepare SOC medium.
Dissolve 29.5 g of potassium acetate in 60 mL of H2O, add 11.5 mL of acetic acid, and then add H2O to a final volume of 100 mL to make the precipitation solution.
Mix 95 mL of 20% glucose with 5 mL of 1 M Tris-Cl pH 8 and 4 mL of 0.5 M EDTA pH 8, then add H2O to reach a total volume of 200 mL for resuspension buffer preparation.
Mix 4.8 mL of 8.3 M NaOH with 10 mL of 20% SDS, and then add H2O to achieve a final volume of 200 mL for the lysis solution preparation.
Prepare the digestion mix on ice by combining 10 µg of pAdTrack-GFP, 5 µL of 10x colorless buffer, 2 µL of Pme I, and H2O to reach a total volume of 50 µL.
Incubate the digestion mix at 37 °C for 3 hours in a water bath.
Inactivate the digestion mix by heating it to 65 °C for 20 minutes.
Add an equal volume of phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1) over the digestion mixture and invert the tube until homogeneous.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 16,200 x g, and transfer the upper aqueous phase to a collection tube.
Add an equal volume of phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (25:24:1) over the lower organic phase and vortex.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 16,200 x g, and transfer the upper phase to the same collection tube.
Add an equal volume of chloroform over the aqueous phase harvested in the collection tube and vortex.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 16,200 x g, and transfer the upper aqueous phase to a new collection tube.
Add a 1/10 volume of 3 M sodium acetate to the collected aqueous phase.
Add 2 volumes of cold 100% ethanol to the mixture and vortex.
Incubate for 1 hour at -70 °C or overnight at -20 °C.
Thaw the sample on ice and centrifuge it for 10 min at 16,200 x g and 4 °C.
Remove the supernatant and add 750 µL of 75% ethanol to the pellet.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 16,200 x g and 4 °C, then remove the supernatant.
Briefly spin the tube to remove all remaining supernatant and dry the DNA pellet in the hood.
Dissolve the dried pellet in 15 µL of H2O.
Measure the DNA concentration using a spectrophotometer (e.g., Nanodrop).
Prepare AdEasier-1 chemical competent bacteria using a commercial transformation kit.
Thaw an aliquot of competent AdEasier-1 bacteria on ice and add 1 μg of purified Pme I-digested pAdTrack-GFP.
Mix gently by flicking the tube.
Incubate for 10 min on ice.
Add 900 μL of SOC medium and incubate for 1 hour at 37°C with shaking.
Microfuge for 5 min at 600 x g.
Remove 900 μL of the supernatant, mix the pellet and the supernatant.
Seed the transformed bacteria on LB-agar plates with kanamycin.
Incubate for ~16 hours at 37°C (do not exceed 18 hours).
Divide toothpicks into two halves and sterilize the half-toothpicks by autoclaving.
Pick up small and translucent colonies using sterile half-toothpicks.
Rotate the half-toothpick with bacteria in 10 μL water (in a PCR tube).
Put the half-toothpick in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 100 μL SOC medium with kanamycin.
Incubate for 4-6 hours at 37°C, while testing the clones by “negative” and “positive” PCR.
Incubate the PCR tubes containing 10 μL water with bacteria for 5 min at 95°C to obtain the bacterial sample.
Dilute bacterial cultures in 4 mL of SOC medium with kanamycin.
Incubate diluted cultures overnight at 37°C with shaking.
Transfer 1.5 mL of bacterial culture in microcentrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge for 1 min at 16,200 x g and remove the supernatant.
Transfer another 1.5 mL bacterial culture in the same tube.
Repeat centrifugation and remove the supernatant.
Add 200 µL of resuspension buffer (50 mM glucose, 10 mM EDTA, 25 mM Tris-HCl pH 8).
Add 200 µL of lysis solution (0.2 N NaOH, 1% SDS), mix gently by inverting the tube.
Add 200 µL of precipitation solution (60 mL of 5 M potassium acetate, 11.5 mL of glacial acetic acid, add H2O until 100 mL), and mix gently by inverting the tube.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 16,200 x g.
Transfer the supernatant in a new microcentrifuge tube.
Add 500 µL isopropanol, mix and incubate for 20 min on ice.
Centrifuge for 15 min at 16,200 x g.
Add 500 µL of 75% ethanol.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 16,200 x g and remove the supernatant.
Centrifuge for 3 min at 16,200 x g, remove the supernatant and add 15 µL of H2O.
Prepare DH5α competent bacteria using the commercial transformation kit, following the manufacturers’ instructions.
Thaw 100 µL of DH5α competent bacteria on ice, add the recombinant DNA, and incubate 10 min on ice.
Seed the bacteria onto LB-agar plates with kanamycin.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight.
Pick-up several colonies and grow each in 2 mL of LB medium with kanamycin, at 37 °C, overnight, with shaking.
Isolate the DNA using alkaline lysis miniprep method.
Resuspend the isolated DNA in 25 µL H2O.
Prepare a digest mix on ice containing 5 µL of recombinant DNA, 1.5 µL of 10x colorless buffer, and 0.5 µL of Hind III or Pst I.
Add water to achieve a final volume of 15 μL for the digest mix.
Incubate the digest mix at 37 °C for 30 min.
Digest pAdTrack-GFP and pAdEasy-1 plasmids as controls with the same enzymes used in the recombinant DNA sample.
Add 3 µL of Sx6 loading buffer with RNase A to each sample.
Run digested DNA fragments on a 1% agarose gel electrophoresis.
Grow a 200 mL culture of bacteria from a positive clone.
Isolate plasmid DNA using a commercial kit (e.g., Qiagen Plasmid Midi Kit).
Seed AD293 cells for adenovirus packaging.
Wash the AD293 cells with PBS.
Incubate the cells with 0.125% Trypsin for 2-5 min at 37 °C.
Collect the trypsinized cells in cold medium containing serum.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 400 x g at 4 °C.
Resuspend the cells in medium with serum.
Seed the cells at a density of ~2 x 10^6/T25 flask.
Digest the recombinant DNA with Pac I.
Mix 6 µL of recombinant DNA (1 µg/µL) with 2 µL of Pac I and 2.5 µL of 10x colorless Buffer, adding H2O to a final volume of 25 µL.
Incubate the mix for 3 h at 37 °C.
Inactivate the enzyme at 65 °C for 20 min.
Add 2.5 µL of (1/10 v/v) 3 M sodium acetate to the mix.
Add 2-3 volumes of 100% ethanol to the mix.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min at -70 °C or overnight at -20 °C.
Centrifuge the mixture at 16,200 x g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Resuspend the pellet in sterile water.
Add 40 µL of K2 Multiplier to the cells two hours before transfection.
Prepare Solution A by adding 6 µg of Pac I-linearized DNA in 260 µL of Opti-MEM.
Prepare Solution B by adding 21.6 µL of K2 Reagent in 248.4 µL of Opti-MEM.
Add solution A to solution B and mix gently by pipetting.
Incubate the mixture for 20 min at room temperature.
Add the A and B mix dropwise to the cells.
Monitor GFP expression by fluorescence microscopy from Day 3 to Day 11.
Collect detached cells and medium in a 50 mL tube on Day 11.
Scrape adherent cells and add them to the same tube.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 400 x g.
Collect the supernatant in a new tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 0.5 mL of PBS.
Transfer the cell suspension to a microcentrifuge tube.
Perform three freeze/thaw cycles (freeze in liquid nitrogen or at -80 °C / thaw at 37 °C for maximum 7 min).
Pass the broken cells through a 23 G syringe needle three times.
Remove the cell debris by centrifuging at 9,600 x g for 12 min.
Transfer the supernatant to the 50 mL tube with the collected medium.
Seed AD293 cells in a T75 flask (5 x 10^6 cells/flask).
Infect ~90% confluent AD293 cells using F1 adenoviral particles: add the cell homogenate and the medium from the T25 flask over the cells grown in the T75 flask.
Monitor GFP expression by fluorescence microscopy.
Harvest virus-producing cells when ~90% of transduced AD293 are detached (~the 5th day after transduction).
Keep the cell culture medium at 4 °C.
Disrupt the cells similarly with those for F1 in 1 mL PBS.
Infect ~90% confluent AD293 cells seeded in T175 flask with F2 adenoviral particles and the cell culture medium from the F2 adenoviral particles.
Harvest the cells approximately 5 days after transduction.
Disrupt the cells in 2 mL of PBS.
Prepare F4 adenoviral particles.
Infect 5 T175 flasks containing ~90% confluent AD293 cells with F3 adenoviral particles and cell culture medium.
Harvest the cells approximately 5 days after transduction.
Disrupt the cells in 3 mL of PBS.
Prepare F5 adenoviral particles.
Infect 25 T175 flasks containing ~90% confluent AD293 cells with F4 adenoviral stock and cell culture medium.
Harvest the AD293 cells after 5 days from transduction.
Save the medium in a sterile bottle for precipitation of the adenoviral particles.
Centrifuge the cells at 400 x g, for 5 min, at 4°C.
Resuspend the final pellet in 5 mL of 10 mM Tris HCl, pH 8 with 2 mM MgCl2.
Aliquot the suspension in 1.5 mL tubes.
Disrupt the cells through three cycles of freezing/thawing.
Pass the cell suspension through a 23G syringe needle for three times.
Centrifuge the homogenate at 9600 x g, for 12 min.
Save the supernatant for adenovirus purification by CsCl gradient ultracentrifugation.
Bring the bottle with saved cell culture medium to room temperature.
Add 121 g of ammonium sulfate to every 500 mL of cell culture medium.
Mix carefully until the ammonium sulfate is completely dissolved.
Incubate for a minimum of 2.5 hours at room temperature.
Centrifuge at 1600 x g, for 15 min, at 22°C and save the pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 4 mL of 10 mM Tris HCl pH 8 with 2 mM MgCl2.
Prepare a discontinuous CsCl gradient in polypropylene tubes for SW41Ti rotor.
Add 3 mL of 765 mg/mL CsCl (high density: 1.4 g/L) at the bottom of the tube.
Slowly add 3 mL of 288.5 mg/mL CsCl (low density: 1.2 g/L) on top of the first CsCl layer.
Gently overlay 3 - 4 mL of adenoviral particle suspension released from the cells or precipitated from the cell culture medium on top of the gradient.
Fill the tubes with mineral oil.
Put the tubes in the cold SW41Ti buckets.
Equilibrate the tubes.
Load the filled polypropylene tubes symmetrically into the rotor.
Centrifuge at 210,000 x g and 4 °C for 18 hours without brake.
Place the ultracentrifuge tubes on a stand with a black paper behind to visualize bands.
Discard the clear upper phase, cell debris, and the upper band in a waste container with bleaching solution.
Harvest the lowest band containing the complete adenovirus (~700 µL - 1 mL) into a sterile 1.5 mL tube and keep on ice.
Pre-wet a dialysis cassette in dialysis buffer (10 mM Tris-Cl, pH 8, 2 mM MgCl2).
Inject purified adenovirus into the dialysis cassette using a 2 mL syringe.
Dialyze overnight against 10 mM Tris-Cl, pH 8, and 2 mM MgCl2 by changing the buffer 3 - 4 times.
Harvest adenoviral stock from the dialysis cassette in aliquots of 10 - 100 μL.
Add sucrose to viral aliquots to achieve a final concentration of 4% for cryoprotection.
Store viral aliquots at -80 °C.
Seed AD293 cells at a density of 2.5 × 10^5 cells per well in a 12-well culture plate with 1 mL complete growth medium.
Ensure even spreading of cells in each well for accurate titer determination.
Detach the cells from one well with trypsin and count them.
Note this number because it will be used to calculate the viral titer.
Dilute the virus stock in complete growth medium starting with a ratio of 2 μL of viral stock to 1998 μL of complete medium (1/104).
Make a 1:10 dilution of the initial mixture by adding 120 μL to 1080 μL of complete medium.
Repeat the 1:10 serial dilutions for ratios of 1/105, 1/106, and 1/107.
Prepare three tubes of each dilution (A, B, C, D) to perform the experiment in triplicates.
Remove the cell culture medium from the wells and add the prepared virus dilutions as indicated.
Monitor the presence of green cells using a fluorescence microscope on day 3.
Collect the cell culture medium together with detached cells into 1.5 mL tubes and keep them on ice.
Add 200 μL of trypsin in each well for 2 to 3 minutes at 37 °C in the CO2 incubator.
Harvest the cells along with the Eppendorf tube containing cell culture medium and keep on ice.
Pellet the cells at 400 x g, for 5 min, at 4 °C.
Remove the supernatant; keep the tubes on ice.
Resuspend the pellet in 250 μL of PBS + 2% FBS; keep the tubes on ice.
Transfer the cell suspension into flow cytometry tubes or plate.
Run the samples on a flow cytometer to record fluorescence of GFP expressing cells.
Seed the target cells ensuring even distribution in the wells.
Detach the target cells from one well and count them.
Calculate the volume of adenoviral suspension required for transduction with the desired number of infectious particles per cell.
Add the corresponding amount of viral suspension to the target cells.
Replace the cell culture medium containing adenoviral particles with fresh medium.
Check GFP expression at the fluorescence microscope.
